subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Tit for Tat Strategy
description: A 60-second lesson on Tit for Tat Strategy.

hook.text: Axelrod ran a tournament of strategies for the repeated prisoner's dilemma. The simplest strategy won: tit for tat.

buildup.text: Tit for tat cooperates first, then copies the opponent's last move. It is kind, retaliatory, forgiving, and clear.

discovery.text: The strategy works because it rewards cooperation and punishes betrayal without being petty or holding long grudges.

twist.text: In noisy environments where mistakes happen, generous tit for tat works better. It forgives occasional defection once.

climax.text: In business and relationships, start kind, mirror behavior, and forgive mistakes. Simplicity and clarity build trust.

punchline.text: Start nice. Copy what they do. Forgive once. Repeat.

quiz.question: What makes tit for tat effective in repeated games?
options: It always defects to maximize individual gain
It cooperates first, retaliates, and forgives
It randomly alternates between cooperation and defection

details.summary: Tit-for-tat is a simple reciprocal strategy: cooperate first, then mirror whatever your partner did last round. Robert Axelrod's tournaments showed this strategy outperforms more complex and more aggressive approaches in repeated interactions.
details.whyItMatters: Tit-for-tat demonstrates that simple reciprocity is the optimal strategy for sustaining cooperation in repeated social and economic interactions. It rewards cooperation, punishes defection, and forgives quickly, maintaining productive relationships.
takeaways: Start by cooperating, then copy your partner's previous action
Tit-for-tat won Axelrod's famous iterated prisoner's dilemma tournament
The strategy succeeds through clarity, reciprocity, and quick forgiveness

faq.question: Why does tit-for-tat beat more complex strategies?
faq.answer: Its simplicity makes intentions clear. Partners quickly learn that cooperation is rewarded and defection is punished. Complex strategies create confusion about intentions, while tit-for-tat's transparent reciprocity builds stable cooperative relationships.

faq.question: How does tit-for-tat apply to business relationships?
faq.answer: Successful long-term business relationships often follow tit-for-tat logic. Companies start with trust, match partner behavior, and forgive occasional mistakes. This simple reciprocity sustains cooperation without the cost of complex contracts.
